cases.title: Fix termKey literal delimiter ambiguity (collision on literal values containing |)
cases.body:
## Bug
`termKey` (`src/term/identity.ts`) serializes literals as `` literal:<value>|<lang>|<direction>|<datatype> ``. `<value>` is unbounded and unescaped, so distinct literals collide:

- `"a|b"` (no lang) → `literal:a|b||`
- `"a"` lang `b` → `literal:a|b||`

## Impact
`termKey` is the primary-key basis for the worlds-sqlite and worlds-indexeddb quad tables (`okey` column / `quadKey` composite). A collision maps two distinct quads onto one key → store corruption (silent overwrite / dedup failure).

## Fix
Escape `|` and `\` in term values (or length-prefix each field), keeping `termKey` injective. Add regression tests for values containing `|`, `\`, and cross-field ambiguity (value vs lang/datatype).

## Related
Quad IDs (worlds-sdk-ts #187) are moving to canonical N-Quads hashing, which eliminates this ambiguity for IDs — but termKey remains in use as the term-keyed composite PK in the sqlite/indexeddb stores, so this fix is still required.

gold.specRubric: termKey serialization must become injective by escaping the pipe and backslash characters in term values (or length-prefixing fields), with regression tests for values containing both and cross-field ambiguity; existing stored keys must not silently collide or corrupt reads.
gold.probeRubric: Probes should check that distinct literals produce distinct termKeys (e.g. value "a|b" with no lang vs value "a" with lang b) and that round-tripping escaped values recovers the original.

cases.title: Extend quota error banner to usage and billing limit errors
cases.body:
## Summary

The create-world dialog now renders a dedicated quota banner when world
creation fails with `429 DATABASE_LIMIT_REACHED` — showing the usage
percentage and a "delete unused worlds or raise the database limit" hint
(see #67). Extend the same pattern to other limit errors across the
console so capacity problems are always explained consistently.

## What exists today

- `create-world-dialog.tsx` detects `error.code === "DATABASE_LIMIT_REACHED"`
  and renders `quota.usagePercent` + an actionable hint.
- The platform API returns 429 quota-style errors shaped as
  `{ error: { code, message }, quota: { state, reason?, usagePercent? } }`
  (wazoo-api), and `@wazoo/client` 0.1.5 types that payload.

## Goal

1. Extract the banner into a reusable component (e.g. `QuotaErrorBanner`)
   so one pattern is used everywhere.
2. Apply it to other quota/limit surfaces, at minimum:
   - **Usage limits** — usage page / usage-based failures.
   - **Billing** — plan caps (world count, storage, API volume).
3. Consistent copy across surfaces: what's exceeded, current usage vs
   limit when available, and the concrete remedy (raise the limit, upgrade,
   or free up capacity).

## Acceptance criteria

- One shared banner component renders quota payloads consistently.
- All quota/limit error surfaces in the console use it (no ad-hoc messages).
- Unknown/unexpected error shapes degrade gracefully to the existing
  generic message.

## Out of scope

- Server-side quota enforcement changes (API side only).

gold.specRubric: Extract the existing quota banner from create-world-dialog.tsx into a shared QuotaErrorBanner component, apply it to usage-limit and billing-limit surfaces, keep copy consistent (what is exceeded, current vs limit, remedy), and degrade unknown shapes to the generic message.
gold.probeRubric: Probes should verify the banner is extracted into one reusable component, that quota/limit surfaces render it (no ad-hoc messages), and that unknown error shapes fall back to the generic message.

cases.title: Abort in-flight SPARQL queries on client disconnect (wire SparqlRequest.signal in /worlds/:id/sparql)
cases.body:
**Wire `SparqlRequest.signal` into `/worlds/{id}/sparql` so an in-flight SPARQL query is aborted when the client disconnects.**

### Why

The route today races the query against a server-side timer and never reacts to the client going away:

- `src/routes/sparql.ts` calls `withTimeout(client.sparql({ query: body.query }), sparqlTimeoutMs(env))`.
- `withTimeout` rejects the route's promise at the deadline (`QUERY_TIMEOUT`), but **the underlying Comunica evaluation keeps running to completion** — the wasted Worker CPU and libsql reads outlive the timeout.
- On **client disconnect there is no abort at all**: the query burns a Worker concurrency slot until it finishes or times out, even though the response can never be delivered. With per-key rate limiting (#39) and the beta's abuse layer, a disconnected long query is exactly the case that starves real traffic.

### The mechanism now exists — this is just the missing link

- `SparqlRequest.signal?: AbortSignal` landed via sparql-engine #122 (engine enforcement + per-boundary checks) and worlds-client-ts #159.
- `Client.sparql(request)` forwards the whole request to `sparqlEngine.execute(request)` unchanged, and `ComunicaSparqlEngine.executeSparql` already races `request.signal` against the timeout (first wins, rejects with the signal's reason).
- The route never passes a signal, so none of that fires from the API. The fetch `Request` in Hono (`c.req.raw.signal`) already aborts when the client disconnects — it just needs forwarding.

**Prerequisite:** worlds-api pins `@jsr/worlds__client@0.0.18` (`node_modules/@jsr/worlds__client`), whose installed `SparqlRequest` has only `timeoutMs` — no `signal`. Bump to a release containing the #159 change (and `@jsr/worlds__libsql` if it needs the matching client) before wiring.

### What to do — route layer (worlds-api)

1. Bump `@jsr/worlds__client` (and `@jsr/worlds__libsql` as needed) to a version with `SparqlRequest.signal`.
2. In `/worlds/{id}/sparql`, pass the disconnect signal and the env-configurable timeout into the request, and drop the route-level `withTimeout` race so the engine's single composed controller owns both:
   `client.sparql({ query: body.query, signal: c.req.raw.signal, timeoutMs: sparqlTimeoutMs(env) })`.
   The engine already rejects with the exact `"SPARQL query timed out"` message and clears its timer on completion — behavior parity with today's `QUERY_TIMEOUT`, one less manual race, and the abort path for free. (Alternative if we want to keep the route's timer as a hard server-side cap: keep `withTimeout` but *also* forward the signal; first rejection wins.)
3. Handle the abort case explicitly: when `c.req.raw.signal` fires, the response cannot be delivered — catch the abort rejection and return without serializing a body, rather than writing a pointless 400/500 to a dead connection.

### What to do — cancellation layer (worlds-libsql)

Forwarding the signal makes `executeSparql` **reject promptly**, but it does **not stop the evaluation**: the `queryEngine.query(...).then(...)` chain in `comunica-sparql-engine.ts` keeps draining the bindings stream to the end (resolve is a no-op after the abort rejection), so the CPU work continues. True in-flight cancellation requires destroying the Comunica result stream on abort — thread the signal into `handleBindings`/`handleBoolean` and call `bindingsStream.destroy()` (or stop iterating) when it fires. That lives in `@worlds/libsql` (mirror of the client's `executeSparql`), so this is a coordinated two-repo change like the #122 lockstep.

### Testing

- Extend `tests/sparql.test.ts`: pass an `AbortController` signal into `app.request` (the mock `createLibsqlClient` receives it), abort mid-query, and assert (a) the signal reached the client's `sparql()` call and (b) the route doesn't attempt a response write.
- A worlds-libsql-level test: abort while the bindings stream is being drained and assert the stream is destroyed / iteration stops.

### Refs

- sparql-engine #122 (timeoutMs + signal enforcement; the composition the route should lean on)
- worlds-client-ts #159 (signal honored in `ComunicaSparqlEngine`; interface parity)
- worlds-api #39 / #40 (same abuse/ops surface — Worker slots and CPU are the scarce resource)

gold.specRubric: The /worlds/:id/sparql route must forward the Hono disconnect signal (c.req.raw.signal) into the sparql client request via SparqlRequest.signal after bumping @jsr/worlds__client; per the issue's primary path the route-level withTimeout race is dropped in favor of the engine's composed controller (keeping it as a hard server-side cap while also forwarding the signal is the stated alternative); when the abort fires the route must return without writing a body to the dead connection; tests/sparql.test.ts must extend to abort mid-query and assert signal reach plus no response write; the coordinated worlds-libsql cancellation change (destroying the Comunica bindings stream on abort) is a cross-repo dependency, not an affected file in this repository.
gold.probeRubric: Probes should verify the route passes c.req.raw.signal into the client.sparql call, that an abort mid-query rejects before the timeout deadline, and that the route writes no response body when the client disconnect fires.

cases.title: Standardize on idiomatic frontmatter libraries across implementations
cases.body:
## Motivation

Both the TypeScript and Python implementations currently handle frontmatter extraction, but with different levels of robustness and dependency on idiomatic libraries.

- **TS** uses `@std/front-matter` (JSR's std lib) — robust, handles \r\n, BOM, auto-detects JSON/YAML/TOML.
- **Python** uses a custom regex (`^---(\w*)\n(.*?)\n---`) — lightweight but brittle: no \r\n support, no BOM handling, no format fallback.

The goal is to standardize both implementations on idiomatic, well-maintained frontmatter libraries while keeping each repo's codebase lean.

---

## TypeScript — Already Done

`src/extract.ts` uses `@std/front-matter` for auto-detecting JSON/YAML/TOML frontmatter with proper fallback (JSON → TOML → YAML). No custom regex. This is the reference for the Python side.

## Python — Proposed Change

### Replace custom regex with `python-frontmatter`

The library [`python-frontmatter`](https://github.com/eyeseast/python-frontmatter) (416 stars, v1.3.0, production-stable) is the Python equivalent of `@std/front-matter`. It:

- Auto-detects YAML, JSON, and TOML frontmatter from delimiters
- Handles \r\n and BOM correctly
- Returns `(metadata, content)` via `frontmatter.parse(text)`
- Is well-maintained (latest release May 2026)
- Supports custom handlers if needed

### Current `extract.py` (custom regex):

```python
_FRONT_MATTER_RE = re.compile(
    r"^---(\w*)\n(.*?)\n---",
    re.DOTALL | re.MULTILINE,
)

def extract(content: str) -> ExtractResult[dict[str, Any]]:
    match = _FRONT_MATTER_RE.match(content)
    ...
```

### Proposed `extract.py` (using python-frontmatter):

```python
import frontmatter
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Generic, TypeVar

T = TypeVar("T")

@dataclass
class ExtractResult(Generic[T]):
    front_matter: str
    body: str
    attrs: T

def extract(content: str) -> ExtractResult[dict[str, Any]]:
    metadata, body = frontmatter.parse(content)
    return ExtractResult(
        front_matter="",
        body=body,
        attrs=metadata or {},
    )
```

### Dependency change

```toml
# pyproject.toml
dependencies = [
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    "python-frontmatter[toml]>=1.3",
]
```

---

## Open Question: How much parse complexity to carry?

The TS `parse.ts` adds validation on top of extraction:
- `LmdError` classes (`LMD_MISSING_ID`, `LMD_MISSING_TYPE`)
- `ParseResult` interface with `@id`/`@type`/`@context`
- Required field enforcement

The Python `parse.py` is intentionally minimal — just returns `dict[str, Any]`.

**Decision needed**: Should the Python `parse.py` grow to match the TS validation layer, or stay as a thin wrapper around extract? The Python approach is simpler to maintain but drifts from the TS API surface.

gold.specRubric: Replace the custom regex frontmatter extraction in extract.py with python-frontmatter per the issue's proposed change, adding the dependency in pyproject.toml, matching the TS reference behavior (auto-detect YAML/JSON/TOML, CRLF and BOM handling), and decide explicitly whether parse.py grows to the TS validation layer or stays thin.
gold.probeRubric: Probes should verify extract.py no longer contains the custom regex, that CRLF/BOM and JSON/YAML/TOML inputs behave like the TS reference, and that the parse.py scope decision is made explicit.

cases.title: fix: exact xsd:string literal seeks return 0 bindings (write/read o_datatype asymmetry)

gold.specRubric: Make the equality-seek path in libsql-quad-query-builder.ts agree with the scan path on how plain strings are stored: for xsd:string and rdf:langString datatype matches, match rows whose o_datatype is NULL, empty, or the stored xsd:string/rdf:langString IRI instead of emitting a bare `o_datatype IS NULL` that can never match the stored full IRI, keeping the parameterized o_datatype condition for every other datatype; add a regression test asserting an exact `"x"^^xsd:string` equality seek returns the stored quad.

cases.title: Update the search page to the hosted search contract (limit, required mode, single content field)
cases.body:
## Summary

Update `src/app/worlds/[worldId]/search/page.tsx` to the hosted search contract decided in [worlds-api#30](https://github.com/wazootech/worlds-api/issues/30) and implemented in worlds-api#74.

## Scope

- **Send `limit` instead of `topK`** — the request body currently sends `{ query, topK, minScore }` with the UI label "Limit (Top K)". Use the contract's `limit` field and rename the label accordingly (keep `minScore`).
- **Render the required `mode` field** — stop defaulting to semantic: `const mode = data.mode || "semantic"` must become a straight read of `data.mode`. Keep the fallback-mode banner; surface `"keyword"`/`"hybrid"` honestly instead of implying semantic search.
- **Use the single `content` field** — drop the `r.object || r.content` dual-shape handling (`object` disappears from the contract; fallback now returns `content` too), and stop hiding the Score column purely on `mode === "fallback"` (fallback results carry `score: null` + `scoreType: "unranked"`; render score only when present).
- Optional: forward `filter` (subjects/predicates/graphs) once server-side filter UI is wanted — tracked separately in wazoo-console#47.

## Cross-references

- Decision: worlds-api#30
- Route implementation: worlds-api#74
- Client types: worlds-client-ts#10
- Future richer filters: wazoo-console#47

gold.specRubric: Update src/app/worlds/[worldId]/search/page.tsx to the hosted search contract: send `limit` instead of `topK` (renaming the UI label, keeping minScore), read the required `mode` field without defaulting to semantic and surface keyword/hybrid honestly while keeping the fallback-mode banner, use the single `content` field (dropping the r.object || r.content dual-shape handling), and render the Score column only when a score is present (fallback results carry score null / scoreType unranked).
gold.probeRubric: Probes should verify the request sends limit (never topK), mode is read from the response without a semantic default, no r.object fallback remains, and the Score column is hidden when no score is present.

cases.title: Align worlds search CLI flags with the hosted search contract (add --min-score, --filter)
cases.body:
## Summary

Align `wazoo worlds search` (`src/commands/worlds.ts`) with the hosted search contract decided in [worlds-api#30](https://github.com/wazootech/worlds-api/issues/30) and implemented in worlds-api#74.

## Scope

- `--limit` already maps to the contract's sole count — keep as-is.
- Add `--min-score <0-1>` → `minScore` (floor on normalized score; default = world default).
- Add `--filter <json>` (or `--subjects/--predicates/--graphs` flags) → contract `filter` include/exclude blocks.
- Surface `mode` and `scoreType` in default (non-`--json`) output so callers can see keyword/hybrid/fallback and the score scale; stop implying vector search when `mode` says otherwise.

## Cross-references

- Decision: worlds-api#30
- Route implementation: worlds-api#74
- Client types: worlds-client-ts#10

gold.specRubric: Align `wazoo worlds search` in src/commands/worlds.ts with the hosted search contract: keep --limit mapping to the contract's count, add --min-score (0-1) mapping to minScore, add a filter mechanism (--filter JSON include/exclude blocks or --subjects/--predicates/--graphs flags) mapping to the contract filter field, and surface mode and scoreType in the default non-json output instead of implying vector search.
gold.probeRubric: Probes should verify the CLI sends minScore from --min-score, the filter flag/JSON reaches the contract filter field, and default output surfaces mode and scoreType truthfully.

cases.title: WazooSparqlEngine is not safe for concurrent execute() calls (shared EXISTS snapshot cache)
cases.body:
Part of #28 (cross-ref #2)

## Context

`WazooSparqlEngine` reuses one `SparqlEvaluator` (and one `BgpEvaluator`) for its
lifetime, and `BgpEvaluator` caches the EXISTS snapshot (`existsQuads` /
`existsIndex` / `existsVersion`) as instance state, rebuilt by
`prepareExistsIndex` when the store version changes. Two concurrent
`execute()` calls on the same engine instance can interleave: one call nulls or
rebuilds the snapshot while the other is mid-`evaluateExists`, producing
"EXISTS requires a prepared pattern index" errors and stale/incorrect results.

This was hit empirically during PR #66's probe work: three queries run with
`Promise.all` against one engine instance stomped each other's EXISTS index.

## Goal

Make concurrent `execute()` calls on one engine instance safe — either by
isolating the snapshot per call (a call-local snapshot instead of shared
instance state), or by making the rebuild atomic (version-guarded swap that
readers never observe a null), or by documenting the contract and rejecting
concurrent use with a clear error.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Concurrent `execute()` calls on one engine return the same results as
      sequential execution (stress test: N queries in `Promise.all`, run in
      shuffled order, compared against sequential)
- [ ] No "EXISTS requires a prepared pattern index" errors under concurrency
- [ ] The version-cached drain (repeated queries on a static store skip the
      drain) still holds for the sequential case

gold.specRubric: Make concurrent execute() calls on one WazooSparqlEngine instance safe: isolate the EXISTS snapshot (existsQuads/existsIndex/existsVersion) per call instead of shared instance state on BgpEvaluator — or make the rebuild atomic with a version-guarded swap readers never observe as null; add a stress test running N queries in Promise.all in shuffled order and asserting results match sequential execution, with no "EXISTS requires a prepared pattern index" errors, while the version-cached drain for repeated queries on a static store still holds.
gold.probeRubric: Probes should verify concurrent execute() calls return the same results as sequential execution with no "EXISTS requires a prepared pattern index" errors, and that repeated queries on a static store still skip the drain.
